newsitem.title: EU: REUTER EC REPORT LONG-TERM DIARY FOR DEC 16 - DEC 31, 1997.
newsitem.headline: REUTER EC REPORT LONG-TERM DIARY FOR DEC 16 - DEC 31, 1997.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS

WASHINGTON - U.S. President Bill Clinton hosts biannual U.S.-EU summit (December 16); dicussions will focus on Bosnia; Central Europe; the Middle East; review of the progress made on the so-called new trans-Atlantic agenda.
December 31, 1996 - Irish EU presidency ends. The Netherlands takes over to June 30, 1997.
THE NETHERLANDS - EARLY 1997 - The Dutch EU presidency hosts conference aimed at defining the future of the Union's relations with African, Caribbean and Pacific group of developing countries (ACP).
AMSTERDAM - Dutch presidency hosts European Council of heads of state and government (June 16-17).
MADRID - NATO holds summit to set the course for enlargement (July 8 and 9).
MONDAY, DECEMBER 16

WASHINGTON - U.S. President Bill Clinton hosts biannual U.S.-EU summit. Main discussions will focus on Bosnia; Central Europe; the Middle East; review of the progress made on the so-called new trans-Atlantic agenda which aims to promote peace and stability across the globe; confronting the new challenges of transnational crime; fostering a healthier environment; and promoting the free flow of trade and investment. Participants include: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton and European Commission President Jacques Santer.

BRUSSELS - Farm Council (To December 17). Draft agenda includes labelling and identification scheme for beef, the status of the new EU veterinary office and veterinary equivalency agreements with third countries.
BRUSSELS - Culture Council.
Provisional agenda includes:
- (possibly) Debate on European funds promoting cinema and television production.
- Directive amending the television without frontiers directive.
- Decision establishing an audiovisual guarantee fund.
- Proposal for a directive harmonising rules on media concentrations.
- Decision on Ariane programme.
- Decision on Raphael programme.
- First Commission report on consideration of cultural aspects of EU action.
- Proposal for a decision on rules concerning the European city of culture after the year 2000.
- (possibly) Green paper on new audiovisual services.
- Proposal for a directive amending directive 93/7/EEC concerning the return of cultural objects unlawfully removed from the territory of a member state.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission hosts conference on "Moving towards the Euro - Strategies and practical solutions for a competitive advantage" (0900/0800 GMT) (To December 17). Agenda includes: the results of the Dublin European Council; which systems should be put in place between the member states that join EMU and the rest?; the stability pact; the role of national central banks before and after the switch to the single currency; the U.K. and monetary union; the strategic impact of EMU on European banking and financial sector; European consumers and the Euro; the impact of the Euro on mortgages and the advantages for consumers; producing coins and notes in Euros and putting them in circulation; the role of European savings banks in the switch to the Euro. Speakers include: European Commissioner de Silguy; Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt; German Finance State Secretary Juergen Stark; Belgian National Bank Governor Alfons Verplaetse. Venue: Hilton Hotel. Contact: EFMA (33) 1 47 42 52 72.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Film Companies Alliance (EFCA) holds news conference to discuss the audiovisual guarantee fund and to present the industry's arguments in favour of its establishment. Venue: International Press Centre (IPC). Contact: Heidi Lambert Communications (322) 732 5546.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Federation of Belgian Businesses holds conference on "The Internal Market: a new action plan" (0945/0845 GMT).
Agenda includes:
- (1010/0910 GMT) European Commissioner Monti gives address on "Internal Market: a springboard towards competitiveness, growth and employment".
- (1100/1000 GMT) DG XV Head of Unit John Farnell gives address on "Summary: impact and efficiency of the single market".
- (1120/1020 GMT) DG XV Director Thierry Stoll gives address on "Agenda for the future: how to improve the functioning of the internal market?".
Venue: FEB, 4 rue Ravenstein. Contact: Mrs Legrand, FEB (322) 515 0826.

BRUSSELS - European Environmental Network (EEN) holds conference on "Environmental regulations in central and eastern Europe" (0815/0715 GMT). Speakers include: UNICE Secretary General Zygmunt Tyszkiewicz; DG IA Head of Unit Marc Franco and Polish Ambassador to the EU Jan Truszczynski. Venue: Kredietbank, Havenlaan 2. Contact: Patrick De Bleser, EEN (322) 510 3231.

BRUSSELS - European Transport Safety Council (ETSC) holds conference on "Increasing survivability in aircraft accidents" (0930/0830 GMT). Speakers include: MEP Mark Watts. Venue: Dorint Hotel. Contact: ETSC (322) 230 4106.

LONDON - Information Society Observatory of the European Institute and the London School of Economics and Political Science holds conference on "Europeans in the information society" (0830/0730 GMT) (To December 17). Speakers include: European Commissioner Bangemann. Venue: The Old Theatre. Contact: Jonathan Barton (44) 171 955 6022.
TUESDAY, DECEMBER 17
BRUSSELS - Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) holds plenary session (To December 19).
BRUSSELS - NATO defence ministers meet (To December 18).
BRUSSELS - EP committee of inquiry into fraud in transit due to hear representatives of tobacco company Philip Morris Europe.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime seminar on "The Dutch presidency of the EU council of ministers" (1315/1215 GMT). Speaker is Dutch Permanent Representative Ambassador Bernard Rudolf Bot. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.
WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 18
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting.
Provisional agenda includes:
- Commissioner Fischler communication on olive oil and olive sector; report on the common market in tobacco.
- Commissioner Flynn communication on action against tobacco consumption.
- Commissioner Brittan communication on relations with Russia in the textile sector.
- Application of the generalised preferences system with Burma.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo and State Secretary Michiel Patijn hold joint news conference on the Dutch presidency's work programme (1600/1500 GMT). Venue: Justus Lipsius building, press room.

BRUSSELS - European Commission holds a multidisciplinary forum on electronic records (DLM) (to December 20). Speakers include Commission Secretary General David Williamson. Venue: Borschette Centre. Contact: Downtown Europe, (322) 732 3520.
THURSDAY, DECEMBER 19
BRUSSELS - Fisheries Council (1000/0900 GMT) (To December 20).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Proposal for a Council regulation fixing, for certain fish stocks and groups of fish stocks, the total allowable catches for 1997 and certain conditions under which they may be fished.

- (possibly) Proposal for a Council regulation amending Council regulation (EEC) No. 3074/95 fixing, for certain fish stocks and groups of fish stocks, the total allowable catches for 1996 and certain conditions under which they may be fished.
- (Possibly) Proposal for a Council regulation laying down certain rules for the access to Community waters of research vessels for scientific purposes.
- (Possibly) Commission proposal on the financing of collection of scientific data.

- (Possibly) Proposal for a Council regulation (EC) amending regulation (EEC) No. 2847/93 establishing a control system applicable to the common fisheries policy (establishment of a Community catch-reporting data-base).
- (Possibly) Proposal for a Council decision on MAGP IV.
- Proposals for Council regulations
a) laying down, for 1997, certain measures for the conservation and management of fisheries resources applicable to vessels flying the flag of Norway;
b) allocating, for 1997, certain catch quotas between member states for vessels fishing in the Norwegian exclusive zone and the fishing zone around Jan Mayen.
- Proposals for Council regulations:
a) laying down, for 1997, certain measures for the conservation and management of fisheries resources applicable to vessels flying the flag of the Faroes;
b) allocating, for 1997, certain catch quotas between member states for vessels fishing in Faroese waters.
- Proposal for a Council regulation allocating, for 1997, Community catch quotas in Greenland waters.
- Proposal for Council regulation allocating, for 1997, certain catch quotas between member states for vessels fishing in Icelandic waters.
- Proposals for Council regulations:
a) laying down, for 1997, certain measures for the conservation and management of fisheries resources applicable to vessels flying the flag of Estonia;
b) allocating, for 1997, catch quotas between member states for vessels fishing in Estonian waters.
- Proposals for Council regulations:
a) laying down, for 1997, certain measures for the conservation and management of fisheries resources applicable to vessels flying the flag of Latvia;
b) allocating, for 1997, catch quotas between member states for vessels fishing in Latvian waters.
- Proposals for Council regulations
a) laying down, for 1997, certain measures for the conservation and management of fisheries resources applicable to vessels flying the flag of Lithuania;

b) allocating, for 1997, catch quotas between member states for vessels fishing in Lithuanian waters. - a) laying down, for 1997, certain measures for the conservation and management of fisheries resources applicable to vessels flying the flag of Poland;
b) allocating, for 1997, catch quotas between member states for vessels fishing in Polish waters.
- a) laying down, for 1997, certain measures for the conservation and management of fisheries resources applicable to vessels flying the flag of the Russian Federation;
b) allocating, for 1997, catch quotas between member states for vessels fishing in Russian waters.

- Proposal for Council regulation laying down, for 1997, certain conservation and management measures for fisheries resources in the regulatory area as defined in the Convention on future multilateral cooperation in the North West Atlantic Fisheries.

- Proposal for a Council regulation laying down, for 1997, certain measures for the conservation and management of fisheries resources applicable to vessels flying the flag of certain non-member countries in the 200-nautical-mile zone off the coast of the French Department of Guiana.
- (Possibly) NAFO: New STACFAC regulations.
- Proposals for Council decisions:
a) Authorising the Kingdom of Spain to extend the agreement on mutual fisheries relations with the Republic of South Africa;
b) Authorising the Portuguese Republic to extend the agreement on mutual fisheries relations with the Republic of South Africa.

LUXEMBOURG - Executive committee of Schengen group on free movement of people meets at ministerial level under Luxembourg presidency. The agreements with the five Nordic countries should be signed. Venue: Kirchberg conference centre.
